title: How did temple communities provision a city?
question: Explore the paper’s community-scale and distance relationships. Output is an archaeological production index, with a separate historical sample showing settlement buildup.

details.description: Explore the paper’s community-scale and distance relationships. Output is an archaeological production index, with a separate historical sample showing settlement buildup.
The curve is a normalized output index. The historical sample is shown in the cookbook; it records buildup without simulating it.

title: Monsoon and state growth
question: Can the documented climate sequence produce a decline in Angkor’s political core?

details.description: We ran 2,000 matched parameter draws at each of three crop responses, plus a neutral-climate comparison.
At the middle response, 1,260 of 2,000 runs decline; their median onset is 1362. Changing crop sensitivity shifts the timing.
The PDSI-to-harvest translation is assumed. Core activity combines court presence and regional population.

title: Can an army return before harvest?
question: How do distance, fish and labour demands change what the landscape can support?

details.description: Six scenarios, each with 32 matched seeds and 18 simulated years.
Moving the frontier from 180 to 540 km adds 40 campaign days and creates harvest overlap in every modeled year.
Unbounded stores mask food pressure in the default setup. Historical quantities still need review.

title: What does a monument persuade people to believe?
question: Can inherited stone keep tribute flowing after military capacity weakens?

details.description: Matched comparisons change how suppliers read stone, elephants and defence.
Default suppliers pledge during failed defence for 7.28 of 12 years on average. Lower trust reduces that to 2.34.
This result tests our belief rule. The numerical relationship has yet to be established historically.

title: Who pays when the court leaves?
question: How do temple bills, court costs and interrupted deliveries affect exit and return?

details.description: The model consumes pledges from the signalling experiment and compares return rules.
With the same interruption, 21 of 32 courts exit. Allowing a funded return brings all 21 back.
Two consecutive shortfalls trigger exit by assumption. Return also depends on assumed funding rules.

title: China’s graduate queue
question: What happens when graduates compete for a limited pool of secure jobs?

details.description: Browser and Python outputs were checked for parity; the app compares the model with the supplied NBS series.
The earlier 2018–22 fit missed the later unemployment bulge. Matching the displayed record leaves the mechanisms open.
The reporting definition changes in 2024. Several labour-market responses are assumptions.

title: School and child labour in Cambodia
question: How might school costs, what school offers, enforcement, migration and the credential floor affect children’s work?

details.description: Policy and reference runs share matched seeds across 12 simulated years; several histories show the range.
The interface exposes differences between policies. Causal policy effects remain under examination.
Programme effect sizes are stylised, and the rural school-retention fit needs a large unexplained adjustment.

title: What keeps students in school?
question: Which explanations of the value of a credential fit Cambodia, Vietnam and China, and who leaves when its relative value falls?

details.description: Human-capital, positional and relational bundles were each drawn 24,000 times against country targets.
Where a wealth gradient exists, adding the relational floor sharply narrows which parameter draws fit.
Cambodia and China lack wealth gradients in this comparison, so acceptance rates cannot rank the theories across countries.

title: Can teacher supply keep up?
question: When do training delays and departures create a teacher shortage?

details.description: An age-structured accounting model follows intake, graduation, hiring and retirement through 2050.
Explore how a lag between training decisions and hiring changes the projected gap.
Starting counts and completion rates are synthetic. This demonstration carries no country forecast.

title: Can a provisioning economy rise and decline?
question: A separate synthetic economy builds fields, waterworks and monuments, then faces a declared climate scenario. Remove one mechanism and compare matched runs.

details.description: A separate synthetic economy builds fields, waterworks and monuments, then faces a declared climate scenario. Remove one mechanism and compare matched runs.
The model is a mechanism test. It has no historical fit score and no claim to identify the cause of Angkor’s decline.

title: When does the court choose another centre?
question: Elites compare staying with a second centre. Workers move under a different rule, while farmers remain attached to their fields. Compare the same economy with movement blocked.

details.description: Elites compare staying with a second centre. Workers move under a different rule, while farmers remain attached to their fields. Compare the same economy with movement blocked.
A court can leave while farming and local maintenance continue. Movement rules remain experimental assumptions.

title: Who can claim the stored food?
question: Compare temple relief and elite extraction in four single-run institutional scenarios.

details.description: Compare temple relief and elite extraction in four single-run institutional scenarios.
Food access differs under assumed relief and extraction rules. Each scenario is one trial.

title: Can the state lose people while settlement continues?
question: Compare relief and abstract barriers to leaving, with people tracked inside and outside state control.

details.description: Compare relief and abstract barriers to leaving, with people tracked inside and outside state control.
State-linked and refuge populations follow separate trajectories under assumed movement rules.

title: What changes when maintenance falls at the same time?
question: The maintenance cut now begins in year 55. Compare it with a maintained system and the bundled elite reshuffle.

details.description: The maintenance cut now begins in year 55. Compare it with a maintained system and the bundled elite reshuffle.
The corrected maintenance-only drought median is 6,209 state-linked people; its unchanged stable reference is 6,958.

title: Who farms, who serves, and who gets fed?
question: Explore the separate extension with bounded labour, paid service rations and an explicit refuge food economy.

details.description: Explore the separate extension with bounded labour, paid service rations and an explicit refuge food economy.
The extension checks annual grain, population and labour balances. Historical rates remain uncalibrated.
